questions.title: Two Sum
questions.description: Find two numbers that add up to a target sum.
questions.question_text: Given nums = [2, 7, 11, 15] and target = 9, what is the most optimal algorithmic approach to find the two indices?
options: A) Nested loops checking every pair in O(n^2)
B) Sort the array and use binary search in O(n log n)
C) Store seen numbers in a Hash Map to find (target - num) in O(n) time
D) Bitwise XOR sum comparison in O(1)
questions.hint: Consider storing numbers in a hash map as you traverse so lookup is O(1).
questions.explanation: A single pass with a Hash Map yields O(n) time complexity and O(n) space complexity.

questions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
questions.description: Find maximum profit buying on one day and selling on a future day.
questions.question_text: Given prices = [7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4], what is the maximum profit achievable with a single transaction?
options: A) 7 (Buy at 7, sell at 14)
B) 5 (Buy at 1 on day 2, sell at 6 on day 5)
C) 6 (Buy at 1 on day 2, sell at 7 on day 1)
D) 4 (Buy at 3 on day 4, sell at 7 on day 1)
questions.hint: You must buy before you can sell. Track the minimum price seen so far.
questions.explanation: Minimum price is 1. Selling at 6 gives profit 6 - 1 = 5. You cannot sell in the past.

questions.title: Product of Array Except Self
questions.description: Calculate products of all elements except nums[i] without division in O(n).
questions.question_text: To compute output[i] = product of all nums except nums[i] in O(n) without division, what technique is required?
options: A) Prefix products pass from left, followed by suffix products pass from right
B) Brute force nested multiplication skipping index i
C) Divide total product by nums[i] using float division
D) Binary search across segment tree leaves
questions.hint: Every index i is equal to (all elements left of i) * (all elements right of i).
questions.explanation: Computing prefix products in one forward pass and multiplying with running suffix products achieves O(n) time with O(1) extra space.

questions.title: Trapping Rain Water
questions.description: Compute how much water an elevation map can trap after raining.
questions.question_text: In the two-pointer approach for Trapping Rain Water, how do you decide whether to advance left or right pointer?
options: A) Always advance the left pointer first
B) Advance the pointer with the smaller current boundary height (left_max vs right_max)
C) Advance whichever pointer has an even value
D) Randomly alternate between left and right pointers
questions.hint: Water trapped at any column is bounded by min(max_left, max_right) - height.
questions.explanation: The water level is constrained by the shorter wall; moving the smaller pointer guarantees the trapped water calculation is valid.

questions.title: Valid Palindrome
questions.description: Determine if string reads the same backwards ignoring non-alphanumerics.
questions.question_text: What is the most memory-efficient way to verify if a string is a palindrome ignoring non-alphanumerics?
options: A) Reverse the string into a new variable and compare: s == s[::-1]
B) Two pointers from start and end moving inward, skipping non-alphanumeric chars with O(1) memory
C) Convert string to ASCII integer array and compute checksum
D) Recursively partition the string into substrings of length 2
questions.hint: Two pointers let you check matching characters in place without creating new copies in memory.
questions.explanation: Two pointers require only O(1) auxiliary space and O(n) time, making it optimal.

questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.description: Find length of longest substring without duplicate characters.
questions.question_text: For string s = 'abcabcbb', what is the length of the longest substring without repeating characters?
options: C) 3 ('abc')
D) 5 ('abcab')
questions.hint: Expand your right pointer, and when a duplicate appears, slide left pointer past its previous index.
questions.explanation: The longest valid substrings without duplicates are 'abc', 'bca', or 'cab', all of length 3.

questions.title: Minimum Window Substring
questions.description: Find smallest substring of s that contains every char in t.
questions.question_text: When implementing Minimum Window Substring using sliding window, when should you contract the left pointer?
options: A) Whenever the current window contains all required character frequencies of target t
B) Whenever the window size exceeds 10
C) As soon as any character from t is found
D) Only when the right pointer reaches the end of string s
questions.hint: Expand right to make window valid, then contract left to find the minimum valid window.
questions.explanation: Once all characters of t are satisfied in the current window, contract left to find the minimal length while keeping it valid.

questions.title: Fibonacci Number (Base Case)
questions.description: Calculate F(n) using recursive tree and identify base cases.
questions.question_text: In recursive calculation def fib(n): return fib(n-1) + fib(n-2), what happens if you omit the base case if n <= 1: return n?
options: A) The function automatically defaults to returning 0
B) It raises a RecursionError (Maximum recursion depth exceeded / Stack Overflow)
C) The compiler optimizes it to O(1) iterative addition
D) It returns the correct Fibonacci value slower
questions.hint: Recursion without a terminating condition calls itself forever until call stack memory runs out.
questions.explanation: Every recursive function requires a terminating base case; without it, infinite frames are pushed to the stack causing a RecursionError.

questions.title: Subsets (Power Set)
questions.description: Generate all possible subsets of an array.
questions.question_text: For an array of n distinct elements, how many subsets does the power set contain, and what is the branching factor of the recursion tree?
options: A) n^2 subsets; branching factor of n
B) 2^n subsets; binary branching factor of 2 (include or exclude each element)
C) n! subsets; factorial branching factor
D) 2n subsets; constant branching factor
questions.hint: At each element, you make a binary decision: either include the element or exclude it.
questions.explanation: Each element has 2 choices (include/exclude), leading to 2^n total subsets and a binary decision tree of depth n.

questions.title: N-Queens
questions.description: Place n queens on an n x n board without any attacks.
questions.question_text: In backtracking for N-Queens, what sets/arrays are commonly used to check diagonal attacks in O(1) time?
options: A) Storing (row + col) for anti-diagonals and (row - col) for main diagonals
B) Scanning all cells on both diagonals using a while loop in O(n)
C) Recomputing Euclidean distances between all placed queens
D) Sorting the board rows after each queen placement
questions.hint: Notice that along any diagonal, (row - col) or (row + col) remains invariant.
questions.explanation: Main diagonals have constant (row - col) while anti-diagonals have constant (row + col), allowing O(1) set lookup.

questions.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
questions.description: Find maximum depth of a binary tree.
questions.question_text: Given a binary tree, which recurrence relation correctly defines the maximum depth of node root?
options: A) max_depth(root) = max_depth(root.left) + max_depth(root.right)
B) max_depth(root) = 1 + max(max_depth(root.left), max_depth(root.right)) (base: empty -> 0)
C) max_depth(root) = 2 * max_depth(root.left)
D) max_depth(root) = max_depth(root.parent) + 1
questions.hint: The depth of any subtree is 1 (for the root itself) plus the greater depth of its two children.
questions.explanation: Base case: empty tree has depth 0. Otherwise, depth is 1 + max child depth.

questions.title: Invert Binary Tree
questions.description: Invert a binary tree left-to-right recursively.
questions.question_text: What is the correct recursive operation to invert a binary tree at node root?
options: A) Swap root.val with root.left.val
B) Swap root.left and root.right, then recursively invert root.left and root.right
C) Delete root.left and insert it into root.right
D) Reverse the order of elements using an array
questions.hint: Inverting means mirroring the tree: left child becomes right child and vice versa.
questions.explanation: Swapping left and right pointers and recursively inverting both subtrees mirrors the tree in O(n) time.

questions.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
questions.description: Find lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a Binary Search Tree.
questions.question_text: In a BST with nodes p and q, if root.val is strictly between p.val and q.val (p.val < root.val < q.val), what can be concluded?
options: A) The LCA must be in the left subtree
B) The LCA must be in the right subtree
C) Current root is the Lowest Common Ancestor (the paths diverge here)
D) The tree is not a valid BST
questions.hint: Since p is in left subtree and q is in right subtree, root is the lowest node where their paths split.
questions.explanation: Because of BST properties, when p and q lie on opposite sides of root, root is their Lowest Common Ancestor.

questions.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
questions.description: Find maximum path sum of any non-empty path in a binary tree.
questions.question_text: When calculating max path sum recursively, why can a node only return node.val + max(left_gain, right_gain) to its parent, rather than node.val + left_gain + right_gain?
options: A) A valid path cannot fork or branch into two children when extending upward to a parent
B) Negative values are not permitted in binary trees
C) Right children always have lower values than left children
D) The parent node can only hold one integer pointer
questions.hint: A path cannot visit the same node twice or branch into two forks.
questions.explanation: A path must be a continuous single line; if a node connects both left and right children, it acts as the peak of that path and cannot extend upward.

questions.title: Number of Islands
questions.description: Count connected components of 1s in a grid.
questions.question_text: In the Number of Islands problem, what is the purpose of sinking/marking visited land cells from '1' to '0' during BFS/DFS?
options: A) To save memory by reducing grid dimension
B) To prevent infinite loops and avoid counting the same island multiple times
C) To sort the grid values in descending order
D) To satisfy binary matrix constraints
questions.hint: If you do not mark visited land cells, your search will revisit them and count them again.
questions.explanation: Mutating visited land cells to '0' (or using a visited set) ensures each connected island is traversed exactly once.

questions.title: Course Schedule (Cycle Detection)
questions.description: Determine if course prerequisites can be finished.
questions.question_text: Using Kahn's algorithm for Course Schedule, which courses are initially enqueued into the BFS queue?
options: A) Courses with in-degree = 0 (no prerequisites required)
B) Courses with the highest number of prerequisites
C) The last course in the curriculum list
D) Courses with out-degree = 0
questions.hint: You can only take a course if all its prerequisites are already satisfied.
questions.explanation: Courses with in-degree 0 have no outstanding prerequisites, so they can be taken immediately.

questions.title: Word Ladder
questions.description: Find shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord.
questions.question_text: Why is BFS strictly preferred over DFS when finding the minimum transformation sequence in Word Ladder?
options: A) BFS uses less memory than DFS in all cases
B) BFS explores level-by-level, guaranteeing that the first time endWord is reached is the shortest path
C) DFS cannot process string nodes
D) BFS does not require a visited set
questions.hint: In an unweighted graph, BFS finds the shortest path first.
questions.explanation: Breadth-First Search visits nodes in increasing order of distance, guaranteeing the shortest transformation path.

questions.title: Climbing Stairs
questions.description: Distinct ways to reach top taking 1 or 2 steps.
questions.question_text: If you can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time, why does Climbing Stairs exhibit the same recurrence as Fibonacci: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2)?
options: A) Because the last step taken must have been either a 1-step jump (from n-1) or a 2-step jump (from n-2)
B) Because stairs are built symmetrically
C) Because 1 + 2 = 3 which is a prime number
D) It is an approximation valid only for n <= 5
questions.hint: To reach step n, you had to come from step (n-1) or step (n-2).
questions.explanation: Every valid sequence ending at step n must arrive from either n-1 (via 1 step) or n-2 (via 2 steps), so ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2).

questions.title: Coin Change
questions.description: Find fewest number of coins needed to make amount.
questions.question_text: In Coin Change (minimum coins to make amount), what is the optimal transition relation for dp[a] where a is the amount?
options: A) dp[a] = dp[a - 1] + 1
B) dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1) for each coin in coins if coin <= a
C) dp[a] = max(dp[coin]) * a
questions.hint: If you use one coin of denomination c, the remaining problem is to make amount (a - c) with fewest coins.
questions.explanation: Taking coin c uses 1 coin, leaving subproblem dp[a - c]. Taking the minimum across all coins yields the optimal solution.

questions.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
questions.description: Find length of longest strictly increasing subsequence.
questions.question_text: In standard O(n^2) DP for LIS where dp[i] is the length of LIS ending at index i, what is the recurrence?
options: A) dp[i] = dp[i-1] + (1 if nums[i] > nums[i-1] else 0)
B) dp[i] = max(dp[j] + 1 for j in range(i) if nums[i] > nums[j]) (default 1)
C) dp[i] = sum(dp[j] for j < i)
questions.hint: Check all previous elements j < i that are smaller than nums[i] and take the maximum length plus 1.
questions.explanation: nums[i] can extend any valid subsequence ending at j < i as long as nums[i] > nums[j].

questions.title: Edit Distance
questions.description: Minimum operations to convert word1 to word2.
questions.question_text: In 2D Edit Distance matrix dp[i][j], if word1[i-1] != word2[j-1], what 3 operations does min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]) + 1 represent?
options: A) Delete from word1, Insert into word1, and Replace character in word1
B) Left shift, Right shift, and Reverse
C) Uppercase, Lowercase, and Capitalize
D) Swap adjacent characters, Split word, and Merge word
questions.hint: dp[i-1][j] corresponds to deletion, dp[i][j-1] to insertion, and dp[i-1][j-1] to replacement.
questions.explanation: The 3 operations correspond to Delete (dp[i-1][j]), Insert (dp[i][j-1]), and Replace (dp[i-1][j-1]), taking the minimum + 1.
